thread:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding Harbor7B (7B, reversible rotary, custom tokenizer) into our int4 flow. Quick smoke: coherent until ~1500 tokens, then starts repeating short phrases and soft hallucinations. seems quant-specific.

devin: can you attach a tiny repro and config? which quant flags?

maria: repro steps: 
```bash
MODEL=harbor7b_fp16
python local_server.py --model $MODEL --quant int4 --preserve-rotary true --max-tokens 4096 --seed 7
# prompt: "List numbers 1 to 2000 then ask for a summary"
```
snippet near 1542:
```
... 1540: "point alpha"
1541: "point beta"
1542: "point gamma"
1543: "point beta"
1544: "point gamma"
1545: "point beta"
...
```
looks like a 2-token oscillation pattern. fp16 baseline doesn't show it.

ori: 2-token loop smells like rotary/headmapping mismatch or a head-interleave bug in our quant packing. do you see any headwise weight permutes during conversion?

maria: convert logs show: "reorder heads: false" and exporter notes "rotary_mode=reversible". our quant tool supports reversible rotary via --preserve-rotary, which i used.

devin: what about tokenizer differences? Harbor export adds a "<pad2>" sentinel and increments some indices in the mid-range. can you diff token ids for common tokens?

maria: i diffed top 5 frequent tokens, they match. vocab_size: fp16=50264, converted=50265 (one extra). remapping with normalize_vocab moved collapse point to ~2760 instead of 1542.

sam: that suggests interaction between vocab index offsets and some circular buffer. grep runtime for modulo ops on ids or any cache keyed by token id. i remember we had legacy snippet in cache_manager: slot = (token_id * 31) % pool_size for jittered sharding.

maria: yikes, found it in runtime/kv_manager.py line 88: # legacy jittered sharding for short ctx: slot = (token_id * 31) % self.pool_size. looks exactly like this.

ori: That would produce periodicity when token ids shift. Also check that reversible rotary implementation aligns head dims — if head order differs then the rotate/sin/cos axes may pair wrong causing two-token cycles. Compare per-head norms between fp16 and int4 after quantization: small script:
```py
w_fp = load_heads('harbor_fp16')
w_q = load_heads('harbor_int4')
print([((w_fp[h]-w_q[h]).abs().mean()) for h in range(num_heads)])
```

maria: ran it. per-head mean diff shows two heads with ~0.12 mean difference, others ~0.01. suspect those two heads are packed differently. converter metadata: "head_pack=interleave_v2" for int4. fp16 exporter used contiguous packing.

devin: ok combine fixes: 1) change kv_manager to index by absolute sequence position not token id, 2) add a head-unpacking compatibility layer for interleave_v2 -> contiguous remap during quant load.

maria: created a PR branch that patches kv_manager and adds an unpacker shim. local tests: repeating prompt length 8192 now passes (no oscillation) for both fp16 and int4. also ran small eval on QA set: int4 EM went from 62.3% -> 62.1% with shim, perplexity delta within noise.

sam: great. @deploybot can you kick off a canary quant build with the unpacker shim and kv fix? link to PR?

deploybot: Canary build started: https://ci.redwood/canaries/harbor7b-int4-7051239999. Status: queued.

ori: after canary, please run headwise bit-compare across the two heads that had higher diff to ensure no sign-flip or byte-order issues. also add a targeted regression test that exercises reversible rotary with interleaved packing + vocab remap.

maria: will add tests and update onboarding doc. filing task ENG-ML-2204 to track remaining validation and perf runs. Thanks all. :shipit:
